description: Machine-readable inventory of testing audit checks: test infrastructure, test effectiveness, test levels and critical paths, and component tests.

statusTaxonomy.partial: The invariant mostly holds, with exceptions, or a soft check shows mixed adherence.
statusTaxonomy.violation: Concrete tests, code, or configuration break the invariant.

enrichmentFlags.description: Run an installed Stryker on the five riskiest source files and grade the mutation score.

relatedAudits.relationship: Owns whether tests, coverage, and end-to-end suites run in hooks and continuous integration.
Owns whether change hotspots are cohesive; this audit judges whether their tests would catch a regression.
Owns whether error paths are handled; this audit judges whether tests exercise them.
Owns automated accessibility scanning in tests.
Owns performance measurement in end-to-end runs.

checks.title: Tests run under a configured runner
checks.rationale: Without a runner and a command that starts it, no test can fail when the product breaks.
checks.expectation: Test files exist, a runner is declared (Vitest, Jest, node:test, Playwright, Cypress, Storybook test-runner, Mocha, or AVA), and a package script runs it.
checks.violationSignal: No test files, test files with no runner to run them, or no package script that runs the suite.

checks.title: No focused or skipped tests committed
checks.rationale: A committed `.only` silently stops the rest of a file's tests from running, and a skipped test checks nothing.
checks.expectation: No `.only`, `fit`, or `fdescribe` in committed tests, and no `.skip`, `xit`, `.todo`, or `.fixme` left in the suite.
checks.violationSignal: A focused test is a violation; skipped or to-do tests are partial.

checks.title: Coverage thresholds configured
checks.rationale: A coverage floor stops untested new code from landing unnoticed, although coverage alone never proves a test checks anything.
checks.expectation: The unit or integration runner sets coverage thresholds, and a configuration or script collects coverage so they can fail a run. Not applicable without a unit or integration runner.
checks.violationSignal: No thresholds (missing), or thresholds that nothing collects coverage for (partial).

checks.title: Tests would fail if the behaviour broke
checks.rationale: A test that stays green when the behaviour its title names is broken gives false confidence exactly where the code is riskiest.
checks.expectation: For each risky module and each pre-filter candidate, a plausible bug in the behaviour the test title names turns the test red: the expected value comes from a specification or a worked example, and the Given could go the other way.
checks.violationSignal: Tests on risky code with no assertion, an expected value computed by the code under test, a Given that never reaches the named case, or assertions that pass when every imported function returns undefined.

checks.title: Mocking only at boundaries
checks.rationale: Mocking the code's own collaborators tests the wiring the test itself wrote, so the test passes when the collaborator is broken and fails when it is refactored.
checks.expectation: Tests fake only what the product does not own: the network (preferably at the HTTP layer, for example with Mock Service Worker), the clock, randomness, and third-party services. Call assertions are kept for effects at a system boundary, and assert the content sent.
checks.violationSignal: Module mocks of the repository's own modules, or tests whose only assertions are on calls to mocks they set up or on values they fed into those mocks.

checks.title: Tests are deterministic
checks.rationale: A test that fails at random teaches the team to re-run and ignore failures, including real ones.
checks.expectation: Tests control time, randomness, and shared state, and wait for conditions rather than for fixed delays.
checks.violationSignal: Fixed sleeps or timeouts, the real clock or randomness in an assertion, order-dependent tests, or state shared between tests without reset.

checks.title: Test titles state the behaviour checked
checks.rationale: A title that names the behaviour lets a reader judge what a failure means and what the test should catch.
checks.expectation: Each test title states an observable behaviour or outcome, not the implementation steps or function names involved.
checks.violationSignal: Titles such as `works`, `calls saveInvoice`, or `test 3`, or titles that promise behaviour the test does not check. Soft check — mixed adherence is reported as partial.

checks.title: Mutations in the riskiest files are caught
checks.rationale: A mutation score shows directly whether the suite notices small changes to the code it covers, which coverage cannot.
checks.expectation: With --with-mutation and Stryker installed, at least 80 percent of the mutants Stryker makes in the five riskiest files are detected. Without the flag or the tool, the check is not evaluated.
checks.violationSignal: A mutation score below 80 percent (partial) or below 60 percent (violation) on the riskiest files.

checks.title: Critical paths covered by integration or end-to-end tests
checks.rationale: Unit tests of each piece can all pass while the flow users depend on is broken where the pieces meet.
checks.expectation: Each critical path, such as sign-in, payment, a primary write, or a refund, is exercised through its real wiring by an integration test (route-level, real database, Mock Service Worker at the network edge) or an end-to-end test.
checks.violationSignal: A critical path, or a top-ranked risky module on one, with no test above the unit level, or no test at all.

checks.title: Data access tested against a real database
checks.rationale: Queries, migrations, and constraints fail in the database, not in a mock of the database client.
checks.expectation: Repository and query code is tested against the same database engine it runs on, for example with Testcontainers or a database service in continuous integration. Not applicable without a database client.
checks.violationSignal: Data-access code tested only through a mocked client or ORM, or not tested.

checks.title: Testing Library lint rules enforced
checks.rationale: The rules catch Testing Library mistakes that make tests pass without waiting for, or finding, what users see.
checks.expectation: ESLint enables eslint-plugin-testing-library with its framework configuration plus prefer-user-event and prefer-explicit-assert, so these rules are on: prefer-screen-queries, render-result-naming-convention, no-container, no-node-access, prefer-find-by, prefer-presence-queries, no-wait-for-multiple-assertions, no-wait-for-side-effects, no-unnecessary-act, no-manual-cleanup, prefer-user-event, and prefer-explicit-assert. Not applicable without Testing Library.
checks.violationSignal: The plugin is not enabled (missing), or some of the rules are off (partial).

checks.title: jest-dom lint rules enforced
checks.rationale: The rules replace raw DOM-property checks with matchers whose failures say what the user would see.
checks.expectation: ESLint enables eslint-plugin-jest-dom's recommended rules. Not applicable without @testing-library/jest-dom.
checks.violationSignal: The plugin is not enabled (missing), or some recommended rules are off (partial).

checks.title: Components tested through what users perceive
checks.rationale: Tests that find elements by role and label and act like a user survive refactors and catch the regressions users would notice.
checks.expectation: Component tests query by role, label, or text, interact with user-event or a real browser (Vitest browser mode, Playwright component tests, Storybook interaction tests), and assert on what the user sees, never on raw utility classes or internal state. Not applicable without a user-interface framework.
checks.violationSignal: Test IDs or DOM selectors as the main way to find elements, assertions on internal state, props, or raw utility classes, or snapshots in place of assertions.
